In [[mathematics]], the '''Weierstrass product inequality''' states that for any real numbers 0&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''x<sub>1</sub>'', ''..., x<sub>n</sub>'' ≤ 1 we have

:<math>(1-x_1)(1-x_2)(1-x_3)(1-x_4)....(1-x_n) \geq 1-S_n, </math>
and similarly, for 0&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''x<sub>1</sub>'', ''..., x<sub>n</sub>,''

:<math>(1+x_1)(1+x_2)(1+x_3)(1+x_4)....(1+x_n) \geq 1+S_n,</math>

where <math>S_n=x_1+x_2+x_3+x_4+....+x_n.</math>

The inequality is named after the [[Germany|German]] [[mathematician]] [[Karl Weierstrass]]. 

== Proof ==

The inequality with the subtractions can be proven easily via [[mathematical induction]]. The one with the additions is proven identically. We can choose <math> n = 1 </math> as the base case and see that for this value of <math> n  </math> we get 

:<math> 1 -x_1 \geq 1 - x_1  </math>

which is indeed true. Assuming now that the inequality holds for all natural numbers up to <math> n > 1</math>, for <math> n + 1 </math> we have:

:<math> 
\prod_{i=1}^{n+1}(1-x_i)\,\, = (1-x_{n+1})\prod_{i=1}^{n}(1-x_i)</math>

:::::<math>\geq (1-x_{n+1})\left(1 - \sum_{i=1}^nx_i\right)
</math>

:::::<math>= 1 - \sum_{i=1}^nx_i - x_{n+1} + x_{n+1}\sum_{i=1}^nx_i
</math>

:::::<math>= 1 - \sum_{i=1}^{n+1}x_i  + x_{n+1}\sum_{i=1}^nx_i
</math>

:::::<math>\geq 1 - \sum_{i=1}^{n+1}x_i  
</math>

which concludes the proof.
